title: Nested Collections
prompt:
Write three functions for working with deeply nested collections:

**Requirements:**
1. `flatten_deep(nested)` -- recursively flattens a nested list to any depth: `[1, [2, [3, [4]]]]` becomes `[1, 2, 3, 4]`
2. `path_set(d, path, value)` -- sets a value at a dot-separated path in a nested dict, creating intermediate dicts as needed: `path_set({}, "a.b.c", 1)` returns `{"a": {"b": {"c": 1}}}`
3. `collect_leaves(tree)` -- collects all non-dict, non-list leaf values from an arbitrarily nested structure of dicts and lists

**Examples:**
```python
flatten_deep([1, [2, [3]]])          # [1, 2, 3]
path_set({}, "a.b", 42)              # {"a": {"b": 42}}
collect_leaves({"a": [1, {"b": 2}]}) # [1, 2]
```
hints: isinstance(item, list) checks if item is a list
keys[:-1] gives all keys except the last (intermediate path)
Handle dicts, lists, and leaf values as separate cases
